children: is holding discussions to acquire or increase its investment in Reflection AI, a U.S. startup focused on developing open-weight models, the Financial Times reported on Saturday, citing people familiar with the discussions.

Talks between the companies are at an early stage, and the structure of a potential deal could take several forms, including a so-called 'acqui-hire,' which allows tech giants to hire staff and license technology, avoiding antitrust scrutiny linked to a full acquisition.
Deal terms currently under discussion were not available. Nvidia
, the world’s most valuable company, has already invested $800M into Reflection, which was last valued at $25B in a

, whose CEO Jensen Huang has in the past called for an open-weight “ecosystem” for AI, could also make an additional equity investment in Reflection or reach an agreement to supply more chips or computing power to the company.
A deal could be reached in the coming weeks, said multiple people with knowledge of the matter, cautioning that companies also could walk away from the talks. Nvidia
and Reflection didn’t respond to FT’s requests for comment.

title: Nvidia in talks to buy ‘open’ model startup Reflection AI: FT
